items.title: Marty Sheller interviewed by Monk Rowe, via Zoom, May 9, 2022
items.q: It was a famous Latin vocalist named Yayo El Indio who had one of those voices.

ctx.x: That’s a memorable statement. I mean I remember stories of Louis Armstrong had to move way back to the other end of the recording — the room where they were playing into a megaphone, right?

Yeah, yeah. It was a famous Latin vocalist named Yayo El Indio who had one of those voices. And when the singers would overdub the chorus parts they were also in a circle and Yayo was always told, “Stand back two steps” because he just had one of those voices that cut through.

You mentioned the Miles Davis that you put away for a year and then you got it out again and you literally had a “bing.” Did you have to have a bing with absorbing the Latin rhythms and sort of getting it inside you?
